title: Terraform compatibility reference and hard‑pinning strategy for Private VPC upgrades
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Background: We need a canonical, machine-readable compatibility reference and an operational pinning policy for Terraform modules and providers used by Private (VPC) deployments. Recent provider bumps caused subtle drift in resource behavior during a small customer's on‑prem upgrade. This ticket defines the reference, pinning rules, CI checks, and rollback guidance to make future upgrades predictable.

Scope:
- Produce a compatibility reference mapping module versions, required Terraform core versions, provider versions, and known migration notes for each Private VPC IaC component (networking, IAM, EKS, inference runtime, secrets).
- Define a hard‑pinning policy (when to pin exact versions vs minimum compatible versions) and how to manage the Terraform providers lock file across platforms.
- Implement CI checks that validate module/provider compatibility and run a lightweight Terratest/plan smoke on a synthetic account.
- Ship a small automation to surface incompatible combinations and open PRs with candidate pins.

Non-goals: Automated in-place state migrations for major provider changes (this will be a separate migration project).

Compatibility reference excerpt (canonical format below; full spreadsheet lives at Confluence link in related_links):
- Component: redwood-vpc-module
  - module_version: 2.3.1
  - required_terraform: 1.4.6
  - compatible_providers: hashicorp/aws 4.68.0 -> 4.74.x
  - notes: "AWS provider 4.73.0 introduced ENI change that requires additional lifecycle ignore_changes when using secondary network interfaces. Tested on staging-1 account 2026-02-22."

- Component: redwood-eks-addon
  - module_version: 1.9.0
  - required_terraform: 1.4.6
  - compatible_providers: hashicorp/kubernetes 2.22.0 -> 2.24.x, hashicorp/aws 4.70.x
  - notes: "kubernetes provider 2.23.0 adjusts default timeouts; add explicit timeouts in module 1.9.1 (patch queued)."

- Component: redwood-secrets-kv
  - module_version: 0.8.4
  - required_terraform: 1.3.9
  - compatible_providers: hashicorp/aws 4.60.x
  - notes: "No breaking change, but provider >=4.65 changes kms encryption context behavior; recommend pin until migration tests merge."

Pinning policy (summary):
- Providers: hard‑pin to exact minor (e.g., 4.68.0) for production Private deployments and update only via the upgrade pipeline. Use the providers lock file checked into infra repo per-platform.
- Modules: pin to exact module semver in Private stacks. For lower environments (dev) allow ~> minor to ease iteration.
- Terraform core: require an explicit minimum and maximum patch window in module README (e.g., 1.4.6 - 1.4.x). Major upgrades require a coordinated rollout.

Operational rules:
- Every provider or module update must go through: compatibility matrix update -> CI plan against synthetic account -> canary deployment in Dedicated staging -> rollout with blue/green or versioned stacks.
- Backout: maintain a tested rollback plan in module changelog and a flagged runbook for statefile snapshots.

Automation & CI:
- New job: infra/ci/compat-checker (runs nightly):
  - checks Terraform init + providers lock consistency for each module combo listed in the matrix.
  - runs tflint, checkov, and terraform validate.
  - runs a terratest plan (no apply) in a synthetic AWS account and reports diffs to a dashboard.
- infra/ci/pin-bot: opens PRs proposing exact provider pins with changelog snippets and notes about required test runs.

Acceptance criteria:
- A machine-readable compatibility reference (CSV/JSON) checked into infra/docs/compatibility/private-vpc-compat.json.
- CI jobs created: compat-checker and pin-bot, green on staging within two runs.
- Documented pinning policy committed to infra/README and referenced in module templates.
- At least two modules (redwood-vpc-module and redwood-eks-addon) validated end-to-end via the new CI checks.

Risks & tradeoffs:
- Hard pinning reduces drift and incident risk but increases maintenance cost for upgrades; mitigation: automation PRs + quarterly upgrade windows.
- Providers lock file must be carefully managed across multiple OS platforms in the CI matrix to avoid spurious diffs. We'll commit per-platform lockfiles and unify via the compat-checker.

Notes on provider lock handling: commit terraform.lock.hcl with platform blocks for linux_amd64 and darwin_arm64 used by our runners. The compat-checker will assert no unstaged changes post 'terraform init -upgrade=false'.

Related test artifacts and dashboards are linked in related_links.
